programme.title: The Fairytale Castles of King Ludwig II with Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank explores the rich aesthetic of Ludwig II. From the mock-medievalism of Neuschwanstein the iconic fairytale castle, which became the inspiration for Walt Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle, to the rich Baroque splendour of Herrenchiemsee, Ludwig's answer to Versailles. Dan argues that Ludwig's castles are more than flamboyant kitsch and are, in fact, the key to unravelling the eternal enigma of Ludwig II.

programme.title: I Am Martin Parr
programme.desc: Examines the work of contemporary photographer Martin Parr, known for his unique and intimate approach to his subjects.

programme.title: Face the Music

programme.title: Art of Persia
programme.desc: Samira journeys to places rarely seen by western audiences to reveal how the Persian Empire was born, the mysterious writing of its early people and how Iran's powerful kings built a vast empire that became the envy of the ancient world.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks
programme.desc: The beautiful outline of Catbells is familiar to all who visit Derwent Water and the Lakeland town of Keswick. By boat and by foot, Julia sets out to discover the secrets of a classic fell-climb for all the family. However, famous views mask a story that is rich in history, miners trod where visitors walk today, when Catbells produced minerals more valuable than gold.

programme.title: The Bermuda Triangle: Beneath the Waves
programme.desc: Scientists embark upon a world-first dangerous expedition beneath the sea to uncover the secrets of the notorious Bermuda Triangle. Laden with sonars and satellite surveys, the divers attempt to investigate the triangle from the bottom up and they make some startling discoveries along the way.

programme.title: Victoria: A Royal Love Story
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce traces the story of one of history's great royal love affairs: the love between Queen Victoria and Prince Albert. It was a love based on a powerful physical attraction, and grew into a marriage that set the tone for the Victorian age. Over the 20 years they spent together, until Albert's tragic death, they gave each other a dazzling collection of paintings, sculptures and jewellery.

programme.title: Smiley's People
programme.desc: Mme Ostrakova was desperate to believe the sweating Russian who promised the return of her daughter. Then there was the Paris letter which rang old bells for General Vladimir. These two events summoned masterspy George Smiley from retirement.

programme.title: Smiley's People

programme.desc: Andrew Marr investigates detective fiction, a genre whose heroes are now embedded in our collective psyche. Andrew deconstructs detective stories by looking at their 'rules', the conventions we expect to be present when we pick up a mystery.
